---
title: "Chemical Search"
subtitle: "Find iBGCs whose predicted chemistry resembles a compound"
---

The **Chemical** search starts from a compound structure and finds iBGCs whose *predicted products* are chemically similar. Use it when your interest is defined by the molecule rather than by the genes — for example, "clusters likely to make something in the same chemical family as my lead compound".

## Supplying a query

Open the chemical chip and paste a **SMILES** string describing your compound, for example aspirin:

```
CC(=O)OC1=CC=CC=C1C(=O)O
```

A **similarity threshold** slider (0.1–1.0) sets how close a match must be. Lower values widen the search to looser chemical relationships; higher values keep only close matches.

## How matching works

Each catalogue iBGC has predicted chemistry — chemical classes assigned to its product by CHAMOIS, expressed in the [ChemOnt](chemont.qmd) ontology. The search places your query compound in that same chemical classification and ranks iBGCs by how closely their predicted chemistry matches it. So a search for a macrolide surfaces clusters predicted to produce macrolide-class compounds, even when those clusters share no genes with any macrolide producer you know.

Because it works from *predicted* classes, treat chemical-search results as a chemistry-guided shortlist to triage further — confirm candidates against their domain architecture and scores.

## Running and reading results

The search runs on **Run Query** as a **background job** and combines with any active filters and domain conditions. Results rank by chemical similarity to your query. Inspect candidates in the [iBGC detail panel](ibgc-detail.qmd) — its "compound features" chip shows each cluster's predicted ChemOnt classes (and curated compounds for validated clusters).
